lines.e1: An exchange rate is the price of one currency in another. If one dollar buys twenty five thousand dong, that is the rate.
lines.e2: We need it because each country's money works mostly at home. To buy from abroad, someone must swap currencies first.
lines.e3: Most rates are set by supply and demand in the foreign exchange market. When more people want a currency, its price goes up.
lines.e4: Demand comes from trade, tourism, investment, and above all, the interest rate a country pays.
lines.e5: When the dollar gets stronger, imports from America cost more in dong, but Vietnamese exports look cheaper to American buyers.
lines.e6: Some governments manage the rate. A central bank can buy or sell its reserves to keep the currency inside a target band.
lines.outro: An exchange rate is just a price.
